questions.question: Describe the Gariep River: its source, two major tributaries, direction of flow and mouth.
questions.expected_answer: The Gariep, or Orange, is South Africa's longest river. Its source is in the mountains of Lesotho, where it is called the Senqu. Its major tributaries are the Caledon and the Vaal. It flows west across the plateau and reaches the Atlantic Ocean at Alexander Bay.

questions.question: Name three rivers that flow to the Indian Ocean and describe one of them.
questions.expected_answer: Rivers flowing to the Indian Ocean include the Thukela, the uMngeni, the Mzimvubu, the Great Fish, the Breede and the Limpopo. For example, the Thukela begins at Mont-aux-Sources in the Drakensberg, plunges over the Tugela Falls, is joined by the Buffalo, and flows east to the Indian Ocean north of Durban.

questions.question: Explain the pattern of river flow in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: The escarpment and the Drakensberg form the main watershed. On the eastern and southern side, rivers are short and steep and flow quickly to the Indian Ocean, mostly all year round because there is more rain. On the western side, the land slopes gently west, and long, slow rivers join the Gariep, which flows to the Atlantic.
